attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter. He is asserting this himself, not quoting anyone.

semantics.note: The claim is a sarcastic aside, but it makes a factual assertion about Cherny's permitted token spend. The normalised wording keeps 'allowed', 'upwards of $130,000' and 'a month'.

contract.note: Reading the claim as permitted usage valued at retail API prices is fair. Using May 2026 is a reasonable choice for the period. The contract also says lower actual consumption would not contradict an allowance, which avoids stretching the claim against him.

evidence.note: A dated secondary post (April 2026) reporting that Cherny posted 7.7 billion tokens of usage. It gives no dollar value, no monthly period and no record of what Anthropic permits, so it cannot settle the claim.

reviews.rationale: The only evidence item reports Cherny's token consumption, with no dollar figure and no allowance. No record from Anthropic or Cherny establishes a monthly permission of about $130k for May 2026, and nothing shows a lower enforced cap. The packet does not settle the claim either way.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: Faithful after the revision. The claim combines a hyperbolic 'nobody', present-tense denial with a causal explanation (pro-AI bias) for why the narrative took hold and moved stocks.

contract.note: The contract lets one functional replacement from 2024-25 contradict a hyperbolic present-tense 'nobody'. It also brings in the next sentence's 'nothing actually happened' as a contradiction route. Neither reading comes from the speaker, and the bias mechanism cannot be measured. The result turns on these interpretations.

evidence.note: Klarna moved Salesforce data onto an in-house stack in 2024-25, before the 2026 narrative. Its CEO says the project only 'started' bringing data together and that most firms won't follow. This is weak and contested as a contradiction of the hyperbolic 'nobody'.

Reuters, Feb 2026: AI-disruption fears and a Citrini scenario pushed software stocks down, and Anthropic announcements lifted some. This supports the narrower point that the narrative moved stocks. It does not show that pro-AI bias caused the narrative to spread.

reviews.rationale: The narrative did move stocks both ways (e2). The causal claim that pro-AI bias drove its adoption is not tested by anything in the packet. Klarna is an older, partial and disputed example, and judging it as contradicting 'nobody' depends on an interpretation the speaker did not supply. The packet does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: Three historical clauses about 2025: combined revenue under $20B, an 89% share, and at least $30B of compute spend with the three named clouds. The normalised wording preserves all three.

contract.note: The plain grammar ties all three clauses to 2025, so reading them as realized 2025 figures is fair. The spending basis is unknown (cash paid vs. expense recognised), which affects how comparable any estimate is.

evidence.note: FT-sourced figure of about $13B OpenAI revenue in 2025. This is only one company; the packet has no Anthropic 2025 revenue figure, so the combined total cannot be tested.

Epoch's estimate of total 2025 compute spend: OpenAI $16.3B plus Anthropic $6.8B, about $23.1B, which is well below $30B. This is material evidence against the claim, but it is an estimate across all compute vendors. The claim's basis is unknown, so it is not a reconciled comparison with spending at the three named clouds.

The 89% figure is the share of annualized revenue among 34 startups in May 2026, a different period and population from 2025 realized revenue. Under the contract it cannot confirm or refute a 2025 share.

reviews.rationale: The combined revenue clause cannot be tested without an Anthropic figure. The 89% source describes a different period and cohort. The compute estimate (about $23.1B total) points against the 'at least $30B' clause, but its basis is not reconciled to the claim's unknown basis or to the three named providers. On these comparability rules, the packet does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: The unqualified 'will spend' and 'will be' make this a scored forecast for 2026. The normalised wording keeps the $765B amount and the more-than-tenfold comparison.

contract.note: Reading 'Amazon's combined capex' as Amazon's consolidated 2003-2017 capex matches his words. The big-tech cohort and the expenditure basis are left unspecified, and the Goldman figure measures the whole AI ecosystem, so how these are defined will determine the result.

evidence.note: Goldman Sachs model (May 2026) estimating $765B of aggregate AI capex in 2026. This shows the figure was a modelled forecast, not realized spending by a defined big-tech group.

reviews.rationale: The forecast covers calendar 2026, which had not ended by the 2026-10-28 evaluation date. No decisive early-resolution event is in the evidence. The only item is the source model's projection, which cannot verify actual spending, so the claim is not yet scorable.
